title: I Let the Aquaponics-Raft Clock Catch the Intern Who Pocketed My Numbered Fry

parts.text: I stepped into raft two at 7:05 a.m. and intern Pia was already using my numbered fry. The board said: ONE RAFT. SEVEN DAYS. FRY STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-nine, system lead, holding a clipboard that listed our cycle. Pia shrugged. "Interns share the raft." I photographed the board, the booking, and her net in my raft. Then I asked for the raft clock. At 7:13 the system desk pinged why Pia's net sat in our raft. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The system desk can see Pia's net in raft two during our cycle.

social.video_title: She pocketed my numbered aquaponics fry — Part 1/2
social.description: Aquaponics raft, an intern in my net, a seven-day clock she posted. I logged the net. Would you have asked for the raft clock?

parts.text: Pia called it culling until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the raft still. The fry went back to my numbered tank. Pia ran a slot of their own and told the next intern atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: INTERNS DO NOT SHARE A BOOKED RAFT. I keep our cycle on a labeled card. Pia brown-bags her nets. The raft finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Raft clock, numbered fry, and a second line on the board. Was culling ever our cycle?
